name: iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max

cameras.label: 48MP Fusion Main
cameras.notes: First iPhone with variable aperture: ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8, ƒ/4.0 (Apple's own spec page, apple.com/iphone-18-pro/specs). The same 48MP sensor also outputs a 12MP 'optical-quality' 2x crop at 48mm equivalent (not a separate lens). Sensor model 'Sony IMX905' and the 1/1.28" format (unchanged from iPhone 17 Pro) are reported by TechRepublic/Notebookcheck, not stated on Apple's own page — treat as unofficial. New 'Apple Reference Image' capability signs sensor data at capture for content authentication.

cameras.label: 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide
cameras.notes: Sensor optical format and pixel size not found on Apple's spec page or in reputable reviews searched; left null rather than guessed. OIS not mentioned for this lens in Apple's per-camera spec text (which does name OIS for Main and Telephoto), consistent with every prior iPhone generation. Also used for macro photography via close focus.

cameras.label: 48MP Fusion Telephoto (Tetraprism)
cameras.notes: Single 48MP tetraprism module: native 4x optical zoom (100mm eq., f/2.8) plus an additional 8x 'optical-quality' zoom (200mm eq., 12MP output) via sensor crop — not a second physical lens (per apple.com/iphone-18-pro/specs and GSMArena). Autofocus type for this specific camera not explicitly restated in the sources found (Apple's Main and Ultra Wide paragraphs each name their AF type; the Telephoto paragraph in the retrieved text did not), so left null rather than assumed. Sensor optical format/pixel size not published.

cameras.label: 18MP TrueDepth (Center Stage)
cameras.notes: Supports Retina Flash and Center Stage framing for photos and video calls. Sensor format, pixel size and eq. focal length not found in sources searched.

computational.name: Photonic Engine
computational.description: Applies deep-learning noise reduction earlier in the image pipeline to improve detail and color in mid-to-low light photos.

computational.name: Smart HDR 5
computational.description: Blends multiple exposures of the same scene so bright skies and shadowed subjects are both well exposed in one photo.

computational.name: Night mode
computational.description: Stacks several longer-exposure frames automatically in very low light to produce a brighter, cleaner photo.

computational.name: Next-generation Portrait mode with Focus and Depth Control
computational.description: Lets the user change the focus point and the strength of the background blur on a portrait after it has been captured.

computational.name: Photographic Styles 3
computational.description: Applies a user-adjustable color, tone, texture and grain preset at the moment of capture without flattening skin tones.

summary: The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max share an identical triple 48MP rear camera system built around Apple's first variable-aperture Fusion Main camera (ƒ/1.48–ƒ/4.0), a 48MP Ultra Wide, and a 48MP tetraprism Telephoto giving 4x native and 8x 'optical-quality' zoom. Both models pair this with an 18MP TrueDepth front camera and Apple's latest computational stack, including Photonic Engine, Smart HDR 5 and Photographic Styles 3.

name: Galaxy S26 Ultra

cameras.label: 200MP Wide
cameras.notes: Samsung states 200MP, f/1.4 (47% brighter than the S25 Ultra's f/1.7) and 23mm equivalent, with binned outputs of 12.5MP/50MP/200MP, but does not name the sensor supplier on its own pages. Pixel size (0.6µm native, 2.4µm at default 16-in-1 binning; also has a 50MP 4-in-1 / 1.2µm mode), OIS and AF type are from DXOMARK's and GSMArena's camera tests. Some outlets label the sensor 'ISOCELL HP2', which is unconfirmed for this generation and possibly a leftover from an earlier rumor, so sensorModel is left null.

cameras.label: 50MP Ultra Wide
cameras.notes: Sensor size and pixel pitch from DXOMARK's camera test; not stated on Samsung's own spec pages. Eq. focal length / optical-zoom multiplier vs the main camera not explicitly stated for the S26 Ultra in sources found (prior Ultra generations used 0.6x), so left null rather than assumed. Not listed with OIS in any source found, consistent with prior Galaxy S Ultra ultra-wide cameras.

cameras.label: 10MP Telephoto (3x)
cameras.notes: Sensor size, pixel size and aperture from DXOMARK's camera test (Tele 1); the 3x optical-zoom figure is Samsung's own stated value. OIS/AF type were not given for this specific module in the sources retrieved, so left null rather than assumed.

cameras.label: 50MP Telephoto (5x, ALoP)
cameras.notes: Samsung's own S26 Ultra marketing avoids the word 'periscope' for this module; Android Authority, SamMobile and GSMArena report it uses a new folded 'All Lenses on Prism' (ALoP) design, ~22% more compact than the S25 Ultra's conventional periscope, with lens elements stacked on top of the prism instead of between prism and sensor. Trade-off reported: longer minimum focus distance (52cm vs 26cm on S25 Ultra) for a brighter f/2.9 aperture (vs f/3.4). Sensor size/pixel size from DXOMARK (Tele 2); sensor named 'IMX854' by GSMArena, unconfirmed officially. OIS/AF type not explicitly stated in sources found.

cameras.label: 12MP Selfie
cameras.notes: Samsung's own pages confirm 12MP and f/2.2 with an 'AI ISP' for selfies; sensor model, format, pixel size and eq. focal length are from GSMArena, not stated officially. Same front camera across the S26, S26+ and S26 Ultra per GSMArena.

computational.name: Nightography
computational.description: Samsung's marketing name for its low-light pipeline across all rear cameras, combining wider apertures with multi-frame noise reduction for brighter, cleaner photos and video at night.

computational.name: ProVisual Engine
computational.description: An on-device processing engine that analyses the scene in real time to sharpen texture and fine detail across the 200MP main photo.

computational.name: Space Zoom
computational.description: Combines the 5x optical telephoto with AI super-resolution upscaling to produce usable images at up to 100x total zoom.

computational.name: Night Portrait
computational.description: Uses an AI image signal processor to reduce noise and preserve natural skin tones in portraits taken in low light, without manual adjustment.

computational.name: Photo Assist (Generative Edit)
computational.description: Lets the user add, move or remove objects in a photo by describing the edit in natural language, using generative AI.

summary: The Galaxy S26 Ultra pairs a 200MP f/1.4 main camera with a 50MP ultra-wide and two telephoto cameras: a 10MP 3x module and a new 50MP 5x module that replaces the previous generation's conventional periscope with Samsung's more compact 'All Lenses on Prism' folded design. All four rear lenses sit as individual rings on a shared raised pill-shaped housing rather than separate bumps, and Samsung markets the system under its Nightography and Space Zoom branding.

name: Pixel 11 Pro / Pro XL

cameras.label: 50MP Main
cameras.notes: Google's own spec page confirms 50MP, f/1.68 and a new, larger 1/1.3" sensor (up from the Pixel 10 Pro) but does not publish pixel pitch or name the AF hardware; those figures are from GSMArena's spec table.

cameras.label: 48MP Ultrawide
cameras.notes: Sensor format, pixel size and eq. focal length from GSMArena's spec table; not itemised on Google's consumer-facing spec page in sources checked.

cameras.label: 48MP Telephoto (5x)
cameras.notes: Google states the telephoto sensor is larger than the Pixel 10 Pro's for ~30% more light capture; GSMArena and 91mobiles put the new size at 1/1.95" (up from 1/2.51"), confirmed as a periscope module. 5x optical zoom with up to 10x 'optical-quality' output via sensor crop; 'up to 120x Pro Zoom' combines this with AI super-resolution/upscaling. A few outlets speculate the module may adopt an 'All Lenses on Prism' folded layout like Samsung's, but Google has not confirmed this, so it is not recorded as a spec.

cameras.label: 42MP Selfie
cameras.notes: Specs (megapixels, pixel size, aperture, focal length, AF) reported by GSMArena; not located on Google's consumer-facing spec page in sources checked. Sensor optical format fraction not given.

computational.name: Magic Capture
computational.description: Analyses roughly 400 frames of a moment using on-device and Gemini models to deliver a well-timed, high-quality 12MP photo, with automatic crop and unblur.

computational.name: Instant Night Sight
computational.description: Captures brighter, detailed low-light photos up to 4.5x faster than the previous generation by combining several short exposures.

computational.name: Pro Zoom (Super Res Zoom)
computational.description: Combines the 5x optical telephoto with multi-frame super-resolution to give 'optical-quality' detail up to 10x and usable results up to 120x.

computational.name: Add Me
computational.description: Uses AI to merge two shots taken from the same spot so the photographer can be composited into their own group photo.

computational.name: Best Take
computational.description: Picks the best-looking expression for each person from a burst of group photos and merges them into one shot.

summary: The Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL share an identical triple rear camera: a 50MP main with a new, larger 1/1.3" sensor, a 48MP ultrawide, and a 48MP periscope telephoto with a larger 1/1.95" sensor giving 5x optical zoom. Google pairs the hardware, set in its signature camera bar, with Tensor G6-driven computational features such as Magic Capture, Instant Night Sight and Pro Zoom up to 120x.
